text: DSH Model Toggle（DSH 桌面插件，Web 设置界面）：为模型设置页补充供应商和单个模型的启用开关，并为第三方模型提供可配置的推理强度选项。它在供应商卡片中显示模型开关，并从模型目录中过滤停用项；还按供应商、模型、接口协议或 base URL 匹配规则，把 reasoningEfforts 与兼容参数写回模型配置。适合需要整理模型选择器或为自定义供应商配置推理强度的 DSH 用户。使用前需安装到 DSH profile；客户端改动后重启一次，无需额外 API 密钥。

DSH Model Toggle adds provider and model switches to DSH's Models page, hiding disabled models from the picker. Rules add thinking-effort options for custom providers by provider, model, protocol, or base URL. Install in a DSH profile; restart after changing the client half. No extra API key needed.

DSH Model Toggle 的功能「Hide disabled models」：包装 DSH 的 modelCatalog() 并过滤停用模型，同时保留其他模型目录数据。
DSH Model Toggle 的功能「Third-party thinking-effort rules」：按供应商、模型、协议或 base URL 匹配规则，将推理强度及兼容字段协调写回已声明模型的设置。

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · dsh-model-controls：Two missing controls for the **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** desktop app, delivered entirely through DSH's own extension mechanisms — the signed `app.asar` is never modified.

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · dsh-model-controls：1. **Per-model and per-provider enable/disable switches** on the **Settings → Models** page. A disabled model disappears from the composer's bottom-right model selector (and the `/model` palette), while its configuration is kept intact and can be re-enabled at any time.
2. **Thinking-effort levels for third-party providers.** Custom `baseURL` providers normally get no effort selector because nothing declares `reasoningEfforts` for them. A layered rule set — keyed on model-id / API protocol / `baseURL` regex, exactly like ZCode's rule table — writes the native `reasoningEfforts` / `compat` fields back into the provider's own settings.

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · What it looks like：A plugin panel inside each provider card on the **Settings → Models** page:

```
┌ Settings → Models ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  myrouter-ds  [custom]  ●                    [Edit] [Delete]      │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  API key / custom settings (base URL, protocol, …)         │   │

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · What it looks like：- **Where:** a block rendered by the plugin's client half into the Models page's own `settings.models.provider-card` slot — the page bundle itself is untouched.
- **Provider master switch:** enables/disables every model of that provider at once.
- **Per-model switch:** one row per model; a switch that is off hides the model from the selector while keeping its configuration.
- **Trade-off:** model rows expose no extension slot, so the switches live in this panel rather than inline on each model row.

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · Platform support：| Platform | Status |
| --- | --- |
| **macOS** | ✅ Built, installed and verified on macOS (DSH desktop, Electron). This is the reference platform. |
| **Windows** | ⚠️ Adapted but **not tested**. The tools now resolve the home directory via `os.homedir()` (so `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop` works), use `os.tmpdir()` for scratch, and auto-probe the usual `app.asar` locations under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\…` / `%ProgramFiles%`. If detection misses, pass `--asar <path>` explicitly. |
| **Linux** | ⚠️ Adapted but **not tested**. Same story: `app.asar` candidates under `/opt`, `/usr/lib`, `/usr/share`, `~/.local/share`. Use `--asar <path>` if none match. |

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · Platform support：The plugin code itself (`lib/`) is plain JavaScript running inside DSH's own runtime and is platform-independent. What is platform-specific is only **path discovery** in the tools, which is why the tools take `--profile` and `--asar` overrides.

> Please report your platform if you get it running elsewhere — the anchor-based page patcher is the only part that can break across DSH versions, and it fails loudly rather than writing a half-patched file.

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · How it works：| Part | Location | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bundle `@local/dsh-model-toggle` | profile manifest dependency (`link:`) + `dsh.profile.bundles` | One package, two halves. The manifest entry is what makes it appear in Settings → Plugins, where the Plugin Manager enables/disables it. |
| Host half `lib/index.js` | same package | Owns the settings namespace `model-toggle` (`disabled: ["provider/model"]`, volatile → persisted into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`). Narrowly wraps `sessionController.modelCatalog()` to drop disabled models from the selector's only data source, and runs the thinking-effort rule reconciler. |
| Client half `lib/client.js` | same package, `dsh.client` + `exports["./client"]` | A `window.__ModuleLoader__` bundle that registers the panel into `settings.models.provider-card`. Reads and writes `disabled` through `ctx.configForms.get("model-toggle")` and reads each provider's `models` from `configForms.describe()`. Registers only while the namespace is served, so disabling the plugin leaves no trace. |
| Bundle patch `cordis.patch.yml` | same package | Inserts the `model-toggle` row. The profile's own `cordis.patch

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · How it works：Nothing in `app.asar` is touched, so the code signature and `ElectronAsarIntegrity` stay valid. The loader composes bundle layers at process start and caches client-module metadata, so **one DSH restart is required after installing or changing the client half**; after that, enabling/disabling the plugin in Settings → Plugins is live.

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · Install：The plugin is a profile **bundle**. `manage.mjs` registers it; the Plugin Manager owns it afterwards.

```sh
cd dsh-model-controls
node tools/manage.mjs status          # what is currently installed
node tools/manage.mjs install         # link dependency + bundle selection + symlink

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · then restart DSH once：```

After the restart, **Settings → Plugins** lists `@local/dsh-model-toggle`: toggle it there. Disabling removes the host half and the panel together; enabling restores both, with no restart. The saved switch states live in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and survive either way.

Uninstall / roll back:sh
node tools/manage.mjs uninstall       # remove the link dependency and bundle selection
```

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · then restart DSH once：`manage.mjs` backs up the profile manifest before writing, and on upgrade from an older install it removes the legacy hand-written `insert:` block from `cordis.patch.yml` while keeping the saved settings. The old whole-page route is deprecated but kept for rollback: `node tools/patch-page.mjs check|install|revert`.

text: @local/dsh-model-toggle README · Field ownership ("what you edit by hand stops following the rules")：Rule output lands in the same configuration layer as the user's own edits in the Models page, so the plugin records what it wrote in `model-toggle.managed`:
section: Field ownership ("what you edit by hand stops following the rules")

text:
@local/dsh-model-toggle README · Field ownership ("what you edit by hand stops following the rules")：- The user layer has no such field and the plugin never wrote it → the rule fills it.
- The user layer's value **equals** what the plugin last wrote → still the plugin's; it keeps following rule updates.
- The user layer's value **differs** (hand-edited) → the field is released; rules never touch it again (mirroring ZCode's *"When you manually change a setting, that setting becomes manually managed"*).
- The plugin's value was deleted → also treated as a hand edit, released.
- A rule stops declaring a field (e.g. the rule was deleted) → the plugin clears the value it wrote and leaves no ownership record, so re-adding the rule can take over again.
section: Field ownership ("what you edit by hand stops following the rules")

text: @local/dsh-model-toggle README · Field ownership ("what you edit by hand stops following the rules")：`compat` is owned **per key**: when the Models page writes back it also returns schema defaults (`chatTemplateKwargs`, `chatTemplateArgs`, …); those extra keys do not count as hand edits, and rules keep managing only their own keys.
section: Field ownership ("what you edit by hand stops following the rules")

text: @local/dsh-model-toggle README · Preview and rollback：**Verified offline by capturing the real request bodies:** on an `openai-completions` route, adding rules is **lazy** — with no level selected the request body is byte-identical to before, and only a selected level adds `reasoning_effort`. On an `openai-responses` route it is *not* lazy: once a model declares levels, pi-ai sends `reasoning: { effort: "none" }` even with no level selected (the predicate is `thinkingLevelMap.off !== null`, and DSH's `off: null` parses as "key absent"). Decide accordingly before enabling rules on Responses routes.

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · full rollback to before the rules were added (including the plugin's written-back fields)：cp ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml.bak-before-reasoning-rules-<timestamp> \
   ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml
```

Deleting a single `rules:` entry is enough for the plugin to clean up the `reasoningEfforts` it wrote for that provider on its next reconcile. To just stop using a level for one model, pick "provider default" / "off" in the selector — no config edit needed.

`probe-request-body.mjs <patch> [level]` boots a real provider config offline with `fetch` stubbed and prints the exact JSON each model would send with and without a selected level — no network, fake key. Run it before adding rules to see whether they change the default request body.

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · Known limitations：- Requires one DSH restart after installing or changing the client half; after that, enabling/disabling the plugin in Settings → Plugins is live. No page re-patching on DSH updates.
- The switches live in a panel inside each provider card, not inline on each model row — model rows expose no extension slot.
- Switches are offered only for providers that **declare models in their settings** (the model list comes from the settings document).
- The effort rule layer likewise only manages providers that declare a `models` list — routes that rely purely on pi-ai's built-in catalog are left alone (otherwise the built-in catalog would be frozen into the user config).
- Write-back replaces the whole `models` array (the settings API replaces arrays as a unit). For providers whose models are already declared in the user config this just adds fields.
- `defaultEffort` (the level pre-selected when a model is picked) is not wired: in DSH that is the route-level `reasoning`, and filling it in would affect the whole provider. The default stays "provider default" (no field sent); you pick a level yourself.
- Disabling the model the current session

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · Layout：```
lib/index.js       host half: settings namespace, catalog filter, reconciler entry
lib/rules.js       rule layer: matching, spec parsing, ownership planning
lib/client.js      client half: the in-page panel registered into settings.models.provider-card
cordis.patch.yml   bundle patch: inserts the model-toggle row

@local/dsh-model-toggle README · Credits：The thinking-effort scheme is modelled on **[zai-org/ZCode](https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode)** (Apache-2.0): ordered level lists plus a level→wire mapping, resolved through layered rules keyed on model id / API type / base URL, with per-model user-editable specs. `docs/zcode-reasoning-effort.md` records what was examined (branch `main` @ `29628c9a`).
